title: Dispatch: c58j per-clause ownership of creature-grant lifecycle and identity hooks + xt6m readiness (attempt 1, Sonnet)
description:
Implements eshyra-c58j plus the readiness half of eshyra-xt6m. Read `bd show eshyra-c58j`, `bd show eshyra-xt6m`, and `bd show eshyra-olc5.12` (DESIGN RECONCILIATION 2026-10-17 and all later notes). Read `bd show eshyra-xwau.1`: its per-clause readiness rule is the PATTERN to follow (activationEconomyOwned in magicItemCompiler.ts). Also read docs/rules-pack-compiler.md and docs/importer-fix-protocol.md, which is MANDATORY because the generated pack changes. Locate code by symbol name.

STATE: the persistent-actor half of c58j is ALREADY DONE. validateItemGrantBinding refuses a persistent-actor grant whose linked actor has no durable campaign actor, and itemGrantSummons.test.ts tests it through combat closure. Confirm this in your notes; do not re-implement it. What remains is READINESS. On the 16 grant-bearing magic items, clauses stay engine-pending on these hooks:
 - F3 'encounter combatant, persistent actor, and owned-entity lifecycle' (16 items)
 - F5 'item-instance cooldown and owned-entity identity link' (16 items)
 - F2 'controlled-entity command action budget' (15 items)
 - F4 'spell execution and summoned entity ownership' (elemental-gem)
Since PRs #665/#669 (merged), the runtime implements a creature grant's lifecycle and identity:
 - start_effect summoning binding with grant identity and variant admission
 - actor links and printed cleanup/reversion/0-HP endings
 - persistent-actor durability
 - as-spell lifetime and the uncontrolled successor
 - grant-ended cooldown anchors
 - bind credits and consumption receipts
 - destroy tombstones
 - retired ids
 - DM-visible provenance
Because of these hooks, use_item on items such as elemental-gem break-gem is refused on the unmodified pack (xt6m).

DESIGN (decided):
1. NO GLOBAL LANDING. Do not add these hooks to LANDED_MAGIC_ITEM_ENGINE_HOOKS: illusion, object and containment grants (deck-of-illusions, feather-token whip, iron-flask) are not owned. Add a per-clause classifier, like activationEconomyOwned, that removes the F3 lifecycle hook and the F5 identity-link hook from a clause ONLY when the clause's scope is exactly a `kind: 'creature'` entityGrant grant (or the operation/effect that exists only to realize that grant) that start_effect binds. Survey the clause representations and state the precise rule in code and notes. Exclude illusion/object grants, iron-flask containment (its F5 containment hooks belong elsewhere), and anything whose lifecycle the runtime does not implement. For example, if a clause carries printed lifecycle terms beyond what olc5.12 implements (owner-command-while-touching, controlled obedience, Staff of the Python's form specifics), the hook stays. List every such case.
2. F4 'spell execution and summoned entity ownership' on elemental-gem: remove it only if the clause's content is exactly the as-spell lifetime/concentration/successor ownership that olc5.12 implements. If the clause also asks for spell execution the runtime does not own, it stays; say why.
3. F2 'controlled-entity command action budget': CONTROL STAYS DM-ADJUDICATED; this is the recorded decision on c58j/olc5.12. Find how the compiler represents a clause the model/DM adjudicates by design (the ADR 0017 hierarchy: model-adjudication). If a representation exists that keeps the hook from counting as engine-pending, move the control clauses there, with a source-faithful reason. If none exists, do NOT invent one and do NOT remove the hook: record that F2 control still blocks readiness, and file a bead proposing the representation.
4. xt6m readiness: report whether use_item break-gem (elemental-gem) and the creature-token operations (feather-token bird) are now ready on the UNMODIFIED pack. If they are not, list exactly which remaining hooks block each, and whether those hooks are owned by another bead. Do not waive anything in production code.
5. Record before/after counts per hook, the newly-ready / no-longer-ready delta (deriveItemOperationReadinessInput / assertMagicItemOperationReady), and the list of operations that became ready. No completeness claim follows.
PERMANENT EVIDENCE:
 - A compiler test re-derives the removal rule over the whole pack: a hook disappears exactly from the classified creature-grant clauses and stays everywhere else, with illusion/object/containment explicitly kept.
 - For every operation that becomes READY through this change, a real-pack conformance test (NO readiness waiver) exercises use_item and then the grant bind/credit/receipt path end to end. That proves the readiness claim is backed by working runtime.
 - Update generated-pack baselines and the hooked-clause invariant without weakening them, as xwau did, and add the thaw note the protocol requires.
VERIFY: run the focused importer/compiler suites, `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`, and `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing.
STOP and record in notes (leave the bead open) if: a clause's content cannot be cheaply classified as faithful-to-runtime or not; F2 control would require inventing a new representation; or a decided point conflicts with code or source.

PER-CLAUSE RULE (magicItemGrantOwnership.ts creatureGrantLifecycleOwned, applied in the classifier on entityGrant clauses only; F3 lifecycle and F5 identity-link hooks NOT added to LANDED_MAGIC_ITEM_ENGINE_HOOKS): owned iff no containment block; runtimeOwner encounter-combatant or persistent-actor; >=1 grant and EVERY grant kind creature; every grant prints >=1 revertOn and EVERY printed ending is engine-computed (duration-ended, one-hour-ended, five-rounds-ended, reduced-to-0-hit-points, concentration-ended; test pins this set to the runtime ITEM_GRANT_REVERT_DISPOSITIONS non-dm-ended kinds). OWNED (7): Bowl/Brazier/Censer/Stone of elementals, Elemental Gem, Horn of Valhalla, Ring of Djinni Summoning.
KEPT (9), hooks stay engine-pending: Deck of Illusions (illusion grant, illusory-entity, not bound by start_effect); Feather Token (object whip grant mixed in + DM-ended endings maximum-daily-flight-distance-reached/owner-dismisses-as-action/owner-incapacitated/owner-dies); Iron Flask (containment block; prints no ending); Figurine of Wondrous Power (owner-command-while-touching and obeyed-owner-command-while-touching are DM-ended); Staff of the Python (owner-bonus-action-command DM-ended; form specifics); Bag of Tricks (next-dawn DM-ended; printed bonus-action command budget); Efreeti Bottle (third-wish-granted DM-ended; outcomes belong to olc5.12.4); Manual of Golems and Pipes of the Sewers (print no ending; the engine's remove-on-end would be an inference). Ring: its 'ring becomes nonmagical if the djinni dies' item consequence is carried in the adjudicated span, judged not an owned-entity lifecycle term.
F2: control stays DM-adjudicated. The compiler already has a representation for that (adjudicated clause with verbatim sourceText; adjudicated clauses carry NO engineHooks by convention, see triage). For the 7 owned grants the F2 hook is dropped from the entityGrant clause and carried by a new hook-free adjudicated clause m4-control-<item> with the verbatim printed control sentence (CONTROL_SPANS in magicItemEntityGrants.ts, integrity-checked). F2 stays on the 8 kept grants that declared it (Deck never declared F2). No new representation invented. (A first attempt that put F2 on the adjudicated clause was rejected: it added 7 rows to the legacy capability backlog, contradicting the convention.)
F4 (elemental-gem m1-quantity): KEPT. The clause is the single-use quantity economy and the hook names spell execution (castSpell effect summon-elemental executing conjure elemental), which the runtime does not perform; the runtime owns only the as-spell lifetime/successor of the bound grant.
XT6M READINESS (unmodified pack): NOT ready. elemental-gem break-gem: m1-quantity (F4 spell execution and summoned entity ownership) + operation effect 'summon-elemental' has no exact trusted readiness clause. feather-token use-token: m1-quantity (F9 variant targeting, movement, capacity arithmetic) + m4 (F3,F2,F5, kept: object whip grant mixed with DM-ended endings) + 'token-kind-payload' has no readiness clause; use-bird: m4 (F3,F2,F5) + triage-stateMachine-op-use-bird (F5 complex item state and duration processing, F9 geometry/targeting/movement/contest). Other vessels: Bowl/Brazier/Censer/Stone blocked only by c1-uses F5 per-period usage reset; Bag of Tricks: c1-uses + m4; Pipes: F5 magic-item-usage-recharge x2 + m4. Follow-ups: eshyra-xt6m.1 (gem/feather effect clause + F4), eshyra-7gkh (per-period reset for vessels/bag).
